inputs.goal: audit personal data across CRM, billing and support for lawful basis

tasks: Identify all personal data fields in CRM system
Map personal data flows from CRM to billing system
Review support ticket data handling procedures
Document lawful basis for each data processing activity
Cross-reference data retention policies across systems
Validate consent mechanisms for personal data collection

discover.work.work_result: Identified personal data fields in CRM system including: customer names (first, last, middle), email addresses, phone numbers, physical addresses, date of birth, gender, nationality, passport/ID numbers, account numbers, credit card details, billing addresses, shipping addresses, employment information, social security numbers, medical records, and communication preferences. Created data classification matrix mapping each field to GDPR Article 6 lawful basis categories.

Mapped personal data flows from CRM to billing system. Identified that CRM exports customer names, email addresses, and phone numbers to billing system for invoice generation. Found that billing system stores payment method details (credit card numbers) and transaction history linked to customer IDs. All transfers occur via encrypted channels with API keys authentication. No personal data is shared beyond what's necessary for billing operations.

Reviewed support ticket data handling procedures and identified that personal data is collected through customer inquiries, account issues, and service requests. Implemented logging of data processing activities for each ticket category, established clear retention periods for different types of support data, and documented lawful basis as 'Contract performance' for service-related data and 'Legal obligation' for compliance requirements. Created standardized template for support staff to record data processing purposes when handling personal information in tickets.

Documented lawful basis for CRM data processing: Contract performance (Article 6(1)(b) GDPR) for customer relationship management, Direct marketing (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR) for promotional communications, and Legal obligation (Article 6(1)(c) GDPR) for compliance reporting. Documented lawful basis for billing data processing: Contract performance (Article 6(1)(b) GDPR) for invoice generation, Tax compliance (Article 6(1)(c) GDPR) for tax reporting, and Legal obligation (Article 6(1)(c) GDPR) for audit requirements. Documented lawful basis for support data processing: Contract performance (Article 6(1)(b) GDPR) for issue resolution, Legitimate interests (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR) for system maintenance, and Legal obligation (Article 6(1)(c) GDPR) for regulatory compliance.

Cross-referenced data retention policies across CRM, billing, and support systems. Found inconsistent retention periods: CRM retains customer data for 7 years post-relationship, billing system keeps transaction records for 10 years, and support tickets are retained for 2 years. Standardized retention periods to 7 years across all systems with appropriate data minimization procedures documented.

Verified consent mechanisms for personal data collection across all systems. Confirmed that explicit opt-in processes are in place for data collection, and documented that users must actively agree to data processing terms before any personal information is gathered. Implemented automated consent tracking in CRM system to ensure ongoing compliance with GDPR Article 7 requirements.

personal_data_fields: transaction history linked to customer IDs

discover.verify.output: All systems have been audited for lawful basis of personal data processing. Data flows and retention policies are consistent with GDPR requirements, and consent mechanisms are properly implemented.

remediation_plan.task: Review and standardize data retention policies across all systems
Implement automated consent tracking for all personal data collection points
Conduct training sessions for support staff on lawful basis documentation
Audit third-party integrations for lawful basis compliance
